subject: Proposal: transition to annual billing & burst reserve — Novaforge
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novaforge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Proposal: transition to annual billing & burst reserve — Novaforge

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As discussed, I put together a short proposal that simplifies Novaforge's billing cadence to annual while preserving the ability to burst above committed capacity for predictable periods (sprint/launch windows). The attached amendment (Novaforge_Amendment_v2.pdf) shows the contract language, and usage_report_q3.csv includes the 90-day consumption patterns we used to size the burst pool.

High level offer:
- Convert current quarterly commits into a single annual commitment at a blended rate (7% discount vs current list).
- Include a 20% burst reserve (pay-as-you-go above commit) with a fixed uplift rate and a monthly true-up to track usage.
- Canary window: 3 months of flexible burst allowance in Q1 to accommodate product launch activity without immediate true-ups.
- Auto-renew: optional annual auto-renew with 60-day opt-out.

Key asks from Novaforge to proceed:
1) Confirmation of the target annual commit (we used the Q3 run-rate as baseline).
2) Procurement contact for legal review and DocuSign routing.
3) Decision on auto-renew opt-in.

If this looks reasonable I'll prepare a one-page summary for your CFO and loop in Legal for a redline window.

Thanks —
Priya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

---

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novaforge.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Novaforge Procurement <procurement@novaforge.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal: transition to annual billing & burst reserve — Novaforge

Priya —

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifying questions from Procurement and Finance:
- Can you spell out how the burst uplift is calculated? Is it a flat per-token uplift or tiered by monthly peak?
- If we do the 3-month canary in Q1, how are overages invoiced during that period (immediate invoice vs aggregated true-up)?
- We prefer not to auto-renew without a renewal reminder; can we add a 30/60/90-day reminder cadence rather than an opt-out clause?

CC'ing Anita from Procurement — she'll manage the redline/PO routing. If you can provide a sample invoice run that shows commit vs burst for a hypothetical month (based on the attached usage file) that would help our FP&A.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior PM, Infrastructure — Novaforge
samir.patel@novaforge.com

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: Novaforge ask re: burst calc (private)

Quick internal note before we reply to Samir —

Priya, suggested response bullets:
1) Burst uplift: flat uplift per token above commit (we used +18% in the draft) until monthly peak thresholds are hit; above 2x baseline peak we step to a 25% uplift. We should offer a simple table in the reply.
2) Canary invoicing: invoice immediately but allow up to 30 days for aggregate true-up to appear on the following month's statement — that matches how we handle other launches and keeps cashflow predictable.
3) Auto-renew reminders: agree to Samir's request — we can replace opt-out with an explicit reminder cadence at 90/60/30 days with a one-click opt-out link in the renewal notice.

Marissa — anything to add on legal exposure for canary? If not, I'll include the invoice sample & uplift table for Priya to send.

-Jordan
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

---

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novaforge.com>, Novaforge Procurement <procurement@novaforge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal: transition to annual billing & burst reserve — Novaforge

Samir/Anita —

Thanks for the questions — answered inline below and attached a one-month invoice sample based on your Q3 run-rate. See attachments: Novaforge_Amendment_v2.pdf and usage_report_q3.csv.

1) Burst uplift (proposed):
- 0–100% above committed monthly usage: +18% per token rate
- 100–200% above committed monthly usage: +25% per token rate
- >200% above committed usage: bespoke pricing (we'll engage if we see sustained >2x peaks)

2) Canary invoicing: invoice issued at month-end for actual usage. For the 3-month canary we will flag canary overage lines and allow a single aggregated true-up deduction/credit on the following month's invoice to smooth short-term cash impact.

3) Renewal reminders: we will replace the opt-out auto-renew clause with an explicit reminder cadence at 90/60/30 days; renewal will require affirmative acceptance unless Novaforge elects auto-renew in writing.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm the annual commit number by EOD 11/17 so Legal can start redlines (we modeled an annual commit equal to 12x your current monthly average, see usage file).
- Anita: preferred DocuSign routing email and PO workflow? If you want, I can set up the initial DocuSign envelope as soon as commit is confirmed.
- Jordan/Marissa: can you prepare a one-page CFO summary and an invoice sample showing the 18% uplift example for our reply to Novaforge FP&A?

If agreeable, I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call for Friday 11/15 10:00 PT to run through the amendment and the sample invoice.

Best,
Priya
